conviction_note: abs_move 7.0 sits a little under the 8.17% option-implied move and well above the name's 3.67% median reaction. p_up is 47 because the stock has sold its last two beat-and-raises (-3.67%, -4.0%), has rallied about 25% off its 9 Sep low into a whisper bar ($3.16) above the top of the guide ($3.09), and has paid downside skew (+3.57). Against that, the construction-software peers that reported in early November were strong. The scaled number (-0.42) is smaller than the findings' sum (-0.9) because the positives and negatives mostly offset; the sum is a ranking key and is not fitted to it.
bar: Company Q3 FY27 guide: revenue $2,125-2,140M, non-GAAP EPS $3.04-3.09 (Q2 FY27 release, https://finviz.com/news/386371/autodesk-inc-announces-fiscal-2027-second-quarter-results, 2026-08-27). Consensus is $3.07 / $2.13B, at the guide midpoint, with an Earnings Whispers whisper of $3.16 (https://finviz.com/news/423384/autodesks-raised-outlook-faces-its-first-test-as-maintainx-joins-the-numbers, 2026-11-16). Chartmill shows $3.13 / $2.176B but I could not verify it (403). No Q3 billings guide: the FY27 billings guide is $8,575-8,650M, and FY27 non-GAAP EPS is $12.52-12.60.
positioning_check: Short interest is about 9.2M shares, 4.4% of shares, 4.6-6.1 days to cover (settlement 2026-10-30, rising), per https://equibles.com/stocks/adsk/shortinterest and https://stockmarketwatch.com/stock.aspx?stock=ADSK (read 2026-11-17). Not a crowded short. The 25-delta skew is +3.57 vol points (downside paid). Put/call open interest is 0.93. The straddle implies 8.73% (8.17% event) against a 3.67% median historical reaction. Earnings Whispers rates sentiment slightly bearish. The stock is at $258.84, up 25% from $206.62 on 2026-09-09 and up 6.9% over 20 days.

findings.finding: Three construction/infrastructure-software peers have reported since Autodesk last spoke on 27 Aug, and all were strong or better. Procore Q3 (3 Nov): revenue +19% (+17.1% organic), organic growth accelerating for a third straight quarter, FY guide raised, RPO +28%, stock +11%. Bentley Q3 (5 Nov): cc ARR +13% and FY ARR guide raised to 12.5-13.5% from 10.5-12.5%. Trimble Q3 (4 Nov): AECO ARR +13% organic. Autodesk's own Q2 construction growth was 'north of 20%'; the market expects Q3 revenue at the guide midpoint.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: ADSK's last two beats on revenue and billings were sold (-3.67% on 2026-08-27, -4.0% on 2026-05-28). Feb 2026 and Aug 2025 beats were bought (+5.32%, +9.09%).
findings.why_not_priced: The consensus revenue of $2.13B sits exactly at the guide midpoint, set on 27 Aug, before these peer prints. If the peer read-through were priced, consensus or the whisper would have moved above the guide top on revenue, not just on EPS. Construction is a minority of ADSK revenue, so the transmission is partial.
findings.independence: Bentley: https://www.bentley.com/en/news/bentley-systems-announces-third-quarter-2026-results/ (2026-11-05). Trimble AECO: https://zacks.com/stock/news/3024760/trmb-q3-earnings-meet-estimates-as-aeco-growth-lifts-revenues (2026-11-04). Three separate companies.

findings.finding: Loop Capital upgraded ADSK from Hold to Buy on 13 Nov 2026 (PT $265 to $310). It cited a reseller/sales-partner survey showing rising growth expectations and stronger demand, plus easing disruption from the new transaction model, while flagging FX pressure in Q3 FY27 and MaintainX integration risk. Jefferies raised its PT from $300 to $325 on 9 Nov.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No baseline record of channel-check reactions. The stock went from $264 on 13 Nov to $255 on 17 Nov after the upgrade, so the note did not lift it.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: it is on the wire. The survey numbers are not public and the stock fell after the note, so the demand signal has not shown up in the price. If it had, the stock would sit nearer its $279 November high, not at $258.84.
findings.independence: Jefferies PT raise: https://www.optionfinance.fr/info-financiere-en-continu/d/2026-11-09-jefferies-releve-son-objectif-de-cours-sur-autodesk.html (2026-11-09). That is a different broker but the same kind of evidence (sell-side). Overlaps in theme with the peer finding but uses separate data.

findings.finding: Nemetschek, the closest listed AEC-design peer, reported Q3 on 5 Nov and fell more than 8%. Its Design segment slowed as fewer maintenance-to-subscription migrations happened (9M Design +7.3%), and Media customers renewed with fewer users (9M Media -1.4%). Management said underlying new-seat demand was unchanged.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a German listing that US software coverage seldom cites. The design slowdown is specific to Nemetschek's subscription migration, and the media-seat contraction affects ADSK's M&E segment, which is a small share of revenue. So it is a proxy and sized small, net of AEC/construction strength elsewhere.
findings.independence: Boersen-Zeitung on the -8% reaction: https://www.boersen-zeitung.de/unternehmen-branchen/aktienkurs-von-nemetschek-faellt-trotz-positiver-geschaeftszahlen (2026-11-05). Same event, so it counts once.

findings.finding: The AIA/Deltek Architecture Billings Index read 44.9 in October 2026, after 44.7 in September and 47.2 in August. That is the deepest slump of the year, with newly signed design contracts weak in every region. Architects are a core ADSK AEC seat base.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The ABI has been below 50 for more than four years while ADSK grew billings 10% or more; no measured reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a macro-to-company proxy, and the company's own number (the Q2 billings beat, renewal rates 'strong') has contradicted it for years, so it is sized small. It deteriorated during the Q3 quarter itself.

findings.finding: Positioning and reaction function point against a beat paying. The stock is up about 25% from $206.62 on 9 Sep into the print. The whisper of $3.16 is above the top of the $3.04-3.09 guide. The last two prints were beat-and-raises that fell (-3.67%, -4.0%; Q2 beat EPS $3.30 against $3.12 consensus and still fell). Skew is +3.57 (downside paid).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 FY27: EPS beat by $0.18 and FY guide raised, stock -3.67%. Q1 FY27: -4.0%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: this is what the skew says. It is filed because the recovery from the September low lifts the bar above the guide, which consensus at the guide midpoint does not show. Short interest is 4.4%, not crowded, so there is no squeeze offset.
findings.independence: Trefis on the September slide (-24% over 8 days, no company news): https://www.trefis.com/stock/adsk/articles/614900/why-did-autodesk-stock-drop-so-soon-after-raising-its-forecast/2026-09-10 (2026-09-10)

findings.finding: The FY28 bridge is a headwind. The CFO said the new transaction model's boost (about 2pts to Q2 revenue growth, about 1.5pts for FY27) will not recur in FY28. MaintainX is unprofitable and the FY27 margin guide was held at about 39% rather than raised, with only a 'modest' FY28 margin improvement signalled. Any early FY28 framing on the Q3 call lands on this line.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Aug 2026 print fell 3.67% when FY27 EPS guidance trailed expectations despite the beat (https://finviz.com/news/386537/autodesk-shares-fall-as-fiscal-2027-earnings-guidance-trails-expectations-despite-q2-beat).
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced by the September drawdown. It stays as a guidance risk because the stock has since recovered about 25%. I have no source that Autodesk gives FY28 colour at Q3, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: Q2 release, margin guide held at about 39%: https://finviz.com/news/386371/autodesk-inc-announces-fiscal-2027-second-quarter-results (2026-08-27)

findings.finding: Unbilled deferred revenue fell 8% and total RPO grew only 2% in Q2 (cRPO +12%), because Autodesk is cutting multi-year discounts (a reseller analyst reports 10% to 5%). That shifts billing toward annual and drags headline RPO and billings optics, but it is inside the guide the company already set.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Disclosed at Q2; that print fell 3.67%, but the fall was attributed to the EPS guide.
findings.why_not_priced: Inside the guidance and already disclosed, so close to zero. Filed because RPO optics can lead the headline reaction.
findings.independence: Avasant on the renewal discount cut: https://avasant.com/?p=285106 (date not verified)

outside_window.finding: The largest enterprise renewal cohort sits in Q4 FY27 (Nov 2026-Jan 2027), so the real test of the FY27 billings guide comes after this window. Q3 commentary on it lands now; the cohort's billings land at the February print.

baseline_tension: The skew and the reaction history lean down, and so does my set on balance. The peer prints after Autodesk last spoke cut against that, so the scaled number is only mildly negative and p_up stays near 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 9 (net of segment): Nemetschek's design-migration and media-seat read cut from -0.5 to -0.3, because it touches only ADSK's design-migration and M&E lines.
Rule 3 (own caveat): the FY28 bridge finding cut from -0.8 to -0.5, since the September drawdown already priced the disclosed non-recurrence and I have no source that FY28 colour comes at Q3.
Rule 6 (inside the guide): unbilled deferred revenue / RPO cut from -0.2 to -0.1.
Sell-side finding trimmed from +0.7 to +0.5: it is on the wire and the stock fell after it.
Peer prints after the company last spoke ('what has worked') left at +0.6; the positioning finding left at -1.0 (no crowded short under rule 7, and it agrees with the skew).
